newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris calls for dialogue in Yugoslavia.
newsitem.headline: Paris calls for dialogue in Yugoslavia.

text.p: Fearing that tensions in Yugoslavia over recent local elections might spread, France on Tuesday urged the authorities to open talks with opposition parties.

"We consider that the current deadlock is dangerous," a French Foreign Ministry spokesman said at a daily briefing. "We therefore again ask the Yugoslav authorities to quickly open a dialogue with the various opposition representatives."
Spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt mentioned strike threats in the metallurgical industry and in transport.
"In such conditions, the Serb government could be confronted in the next few days with a widening of the protest movement if it does not swiftly move to make the necessary opening gestures," he said.

Serbian opposition parties boycotted the Yugoslav federal parliament on Tuesday, vowing to stay away until Serbia's President Slobodan Milosevic acknowledged he had cheated them of local election victories last month.

Their boycott of the first post-election session of parliament came as NATO foreign ministers meeting in Brussels called on Milosevic to revoke the cancellation of municipal poll results which the opposition said it had won.

"No clarification has yet been made on the reasons for the cancellation of the results of the second round of the municipal elections", Rummelhardt said. "Yet this clarification is absolutely necessary."
